title: PCB Bans All-Rounder Hamza Nazar for Two Years Over Misleading Visa Application
excerpt: The Pakistan Cricket Board also fined the young cricketer PKR 1 million after an internal inquiry found he provided false information during a visa application.
body:
• Pakistan Cricket Board banned all-rounder Hamza Nazar from all domestic and international cricket for two years
  • Nazar was also fined PKR 1 million (roughly $3,500) after an internal disciplinary inquiry
  • The PCB found he provided misleading and incomplete information during a visa application
  • The board said it takes cases of misrepresentation and non-disclosure "very seriously"

The Pakistan Cricket Board has banned all-rounder Hamza Nazar from all forms of cricket for two years and imposed a fine of PKR 1 million following a disciplinary inquiry that found he provided misleading information during a visa application.

The PCB's Findings

The decision, announced on Thursday, came after the PCB conducted an internal investigation into Nazar's conduct. According to the board, the inquiry concluded that Nazar had provided "misleading and incomplete information" during a visa application, with his actions amounting to misrepresentation and non-disclosure.

""The PCB takes cases of misrepresentation and non-disclosure very seriously," the board said in a statement, as reported by the Times of India and Dawn."

The two-year ban covers all domestic and international cricket activities, effectively sidelining the young all-rounder through 2028. The PKR 1 million fine — roughly $3,500 — adds a financial penalty to the suspension.

A Pattern of Disciplinary Action

The Nazar case is the latest in a series of disciplinary actions by the PCB in 2026. Earlier this year, spinner Mohammad Nawaz accepted a three-month anti-doping sanction after testing positive for a prohibited substance during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup. Fast bowlers Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Abbas were also penalized by the ICC for breaching the code of conduct during the West Indies Test series.

The visa-related nature of Nazar's ban is unusual in cricket disciplinary proceedings, where bans more commonly stem from anti-corruption or anti-doping violations. The PCB did not specify the destination country for the visa application or the exact nature of the misleading information provided.

Implications for Pakistan Cricket

Nazar's ban comes at a time when Pakistan cricket is navigating complex relationships with international leagues and overseas opportunities. The PCB has previously clashed with players over No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for participation in foreign T20 leagues, and last year briefly suspended all player NOCs following Pakistan's defeat in the Asia Cup final.

The board's decision to impose a two-year ban — rather than the shorter suspensions typically seen for administrative violations — signals an intent to deter future misconduct related to visa and travel documentation.

For Nazar, the ban represents a significant setback to his nascent career. The all-rounder will be ineligible for all PCB-sanctioned cricket until 2028, missing key domestic tournaments including the Pakistan Super League and any potential international call-ups.
